newsitem.title: UK: JKX sets 2-for-3 rights issue at 34p/share.
newsitem.headline: JKX sets 2-for-3 rights issue at 34p/share.

text.p: British oil exploration company JKX Oil & Gas plc said on Friday it planned a two-for-three rights issue at a price of 34p intended to raise about 14.2 million stg.
The issue is fully underwritten by Guinness Mahon. News of the issue came after the company's shares closed 1-1/2 pence higher at 90-1/2.

The company said the funding requirement stemmed from a need for extra working capital due to slower-than-expected gas sales in the Ukraine, and to fund capital expenditure in both the Ukraine and Georgia.
JKX works in the Ukraine through the Poltava Petroleum Company (PPC), in which it has a 49 percent stake.

PPC is suffering from changes in the Ukrainian gas distribution market, which made it impossible for PPC's main client to pay for its gas. The Ukrainian government, which does not allow export of gas, did not recognise this company as an official distributor.

Deliveries were suspended in June, leaving PPC with unsold gas. Sales resumed in September, but the payments from the new customer, Itera, are coming in up to 60 days after the contractual agreed date.
PPC is meanwhile seeking buyers for the gas it has still storage and for the uncommitted gas it will produce this year.
JKX made a 1.6 million stg provision for the unsold gas.
On top of this, PPC's production in December failed to meet the target set out in the 1995 report because of disappointing results from four commitment wells.
Consequently, JKX needs extra working capital, also to fund its capital expenditure programme on its existing portfolio of assets in the Ukraine and Georgia.

Asked whether Ukrainian business conditions were becoming less volatile, JKX managing director Robert McCrackin said: "There is no predictable course. That is the risk that we have." "We're building in a gas market that is very diffuclt, but there is a huge need for gas," he added.
